Chariots

precepts.text: Who maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud the Lord descended in is His vehicle of travel.
precepts.point: And that will by no means clear the guilty: He will forgive you, but you will still be judged; He still visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children and upon the children's children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.

note.label: Exodus 34: The Second Tables and the Covenant Renewed

precepts.why:
“And the Lord descended in the cloud, and stood with him there”. “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind”.

The clouds are His chariot, His vehicle, His way of traveling. The cloud the Lord descended in on the mount is His vehicle of travel; the Most High, Christ and the angels travel in these vehicles.

precepts.text: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire; the cloud and fire were His created spirits.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire”.

The cloud and the fire upon the tabernacle speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels. He makes the clouds His chariot, and He makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flaming fire; the cloud by day and the fire by night in the sight of all the house of Israel were His created spirits.

precepts.text: The rocks are a refuge for the conies; the coney is the rock dwelling pika.
precepts.point: Their carcase shall ye not touch sits inside the dietary law: it goes into sacrificing the unclean thing and eating it, touching it with the mouth. It does not mean a dead animal in your path cannot be moved out of the way with the hands; the tabernacle itself had to be built by hand with badgers' skins.

note.label: Leviticus 11: The Dietary Law of Clean and Unclean Beasts

precepts.why:
The coney “cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof; he is unclean unto you.” The coney is the pika, a small mountain dwelling mammal that resembles its close relative the rabbit, found at heights among the highest of any mammal.

The scriptures already had it right: “The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats; and the rocks for the conies.” A rock dwelling animal of the high hills, exactly where the pika lives.

Whatever it is called, it has only the one mark, chewing the cud, and not the divided hoof. Both marks must be present, so you cannot eat coney, and the hare likewise is unclean.

precepts.text: He maketh the clouds his chariot; the cloud over the tabernacle was his chariot.
precepts.point: That cloud is the chariot of the Most High: he maketh the clouds his chariot, and that is what sat over the top of the tabernacle.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
On the day the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered it, “and at even there was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until the morning.” That cloud is the chariot of the Most High: “Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind.”

He maketh the clouds his chariot, and that is what sat over the top of the tabernacle, the cloud by day and the appearance of fire by night.

precepts.text: He maketh the clouds his chariot and his angels spirits, his ministers a flaming fire.
precepts.point: Flood your mind with spiritual songs that prophesy within the music, like the albums coming out on Original Royalty, because the Most High wants to hear righteous songs, not the noise of the world.

note.label: Psalm 47: God the Great King Over All the Earth

precepts.why:
“God is gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.” Psalm 104 shows what he rides in and who comes with him: he “maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire”.

The clouds Christ comes with are his chariots. The angels are made spirits and his ministers a flaming fire, and the nuclear destruction coming on the kingdoms of the earth is the fire Christ appears with as he renders his anger with fury. That is the King of all the earth we sing praises to with understanding.

precepts.text: The lights of heaven are for signs and seasons, days and years.
precepts.point: He makes His angels spirits and His ministers a flaming fire.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain”. The Most High stretched out the heavens, and he set the lights in them.

“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. The lights of heaven are for signs and seasons, days and years. They were set in the heavens he stretched out like a curtain, by the one clothed with honour and majesty.

David blesses him for it: the heavens, the lights in them, the clouds his chariot, the wings of the wind he walks upon, all his creation.

precepts.text: Wine drunk moderately is as good as life and makes men glad, but with excess it brings bitterness.
precepts.point: Wine makes glad the heart of man and oil makes his face to shine. This shows we are dark-skinned people, for oil is put on dry skin to make it shine, and the scriptures describe us.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man’s heart.” Wine makes glad the heart of man, and Ecclesiasticus says how: “Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.”

Wine drunk moderately is as good as life and was made to make men glad. “Wine measurably drunk and in season bringeth gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind: But wine drunken with excess maketh bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.” Measurably and in season it brings gladness of the heart; with excess it brings bitterness, brawling and quarrelling.

So the wine that makes glad the heart of man is wine drunk in measure. The Most High brought it out of the earth for gladness, not for excess.

precepts.text: The moon marks the seasons and the appointed feasts.
precepts.point: He makes darkness and it is night, wherein the beasts of the forest and the young lions seek their meat from God; the night belongs to the beasts, the day belongs to man who goes to his labor until evening.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“He appointed the moon for seasons”. Ecclesiasticus gives the reason: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

“From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon does not only mark the seasons; it marks the appointed feasts of the Most High. That is the office he gave it in the creation, alongside the sun that “knoweth his going down”, the darkness he makes for the beasts of the forest and the day he gives to man for his labour until the evening.

precepts.text: Man and beast have one departure; the body returns to dust, but our spirit returns to the Most High.
precepts.point: When He takes away their breath they die and return to their dust; when He sends forth His spirit they are created and He renews the face of the earth.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust.” Solomon says the same of man and beast together: “as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all is vanity.”

“All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.” Man and beast have one departure. The body goes back to the dust it came from, but our spirit returns to the Most High who sent it forth.

So the psalm speaks of every creature, small and great, that waits upon him for their meat in due season: he opens his hand and they are filled with good, he hides his face and they are troubled, he takes away their breath and they die, and he sends forth his spirit and they are created, and he renews the face of the earth.

precepts.text: By the rivers of Babylon our captors required a song of Zion, but how shall we sing the Lord's song in a strange land?
precepts.point: He prays the wicked be consumed from the earth, and again charges his soul to bless the Lord.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
David resolves, “I will sing unto the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.” Psalm 137 shows what became of that song in captivity: “By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yea, we wept, when we remembered Zion. We hanged our harps upon the willows in the midst thereof.”

“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” Our captors wanted the songs of Zion for their own entertainment. The answer was a question: “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?”

That is the difference between the psalmist singing to the Most High while he has his being, and a captive people whose harps hang on the willows in a strange land.

precepts.text: As Israel repents and returns, righteous songs of praise are rising again in place of the songs of captivity.
precepts.point: He prays the wicked be consumed from the earth, and again charges his soul to bless the Lord.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“Take thou away from me the noise of thy songs; for I will not hear the melody of thy viols.” The songs of a rebellious Israel were noise to the Most High; he would not hear them.

Set that against David: “My meditation of him shall be sweet: I will be glad in the Lord.” The song he accepts comes from the one whose meditation is of him, who prays that the sinners be consumed out of the earth and the wicked be no more, and who charges his own soul, “Bless thou the Lord, O my soul.”

As Israel repents and returns, righteous songs of praise are rising again in place of the songs of captivity, songs the Most High will hear.

precepts.text: The Most High covers Himself with light, stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and makes the clouds His chariot, walking upon the wings of the wind, so the spirit riding in the chariot is the Lord.
precepts.point: The lesson is that the Most High wants us on one accord, moving when He moves and standing when He stands, just as the powers of heaven do only what He commands.

note.label: Ezekiel 1: The Vision by the River Chebar

precepts.why:
“O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty. Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind”.

The Most High makes the clouds His chariot and walks upon the wings of the wind. So the wheels Ezekiel saw by the living creatures, the wheel in the middle of a wheel, are chariots, and this answers who rides in them: the spirit riding in the chariot is the Lord. “Whithersoever the spirit was to go, they went”, for “the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.”

precepts.text: He layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters and maketh the clouds his chariot; the clouds are his chariots.
precepts.point: The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“While they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.” He was taken up in the middle of his speaking, after forty days. That was the exit.

The Most High “maketh the clouds his chariot.” So this was not merely a cloud but a chariot, an instrument of the angels, the same as the moon is an instrument of the armies above. Christ was received up by a chariot, not carried by little white angels in the clouds as the Christian movies depict.

The kind of chariot that masks itself in a cloud was seen in 2011 over the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem: a glowing orb that descended and then shot off at about four thousand miles an hour over one of the most secure no-fly zones in the world, witnessed by thousands and reported internationally.
